modern: So the dispute, he said, is not about any ordinary matter, but about being mad or not.
original: The dispute then, he said, is not about any common matter, but about being mad or not.

explained.summary: Epictetus, on why these questions matter: the argument isn’t about some trivial point but about whether you’re sane or not. Getting your judgements and values right isn’t a hobby for philosophers. In Stoic terms, living by false opinions is a kind of madness, so the stakes couldn’t be higher.
